title: Slate Prime Launch Readiness and Dependency Surgery
next_steps: Share trimmed benchmark CSV + latency percentiles (Ravi) by Mon 1/11
Post the dependency truncation plan to #launch-readiness (Lena) by EOD Tue 1/12
Schedule rollback drill with oncall roster (Sofia) week of 1/18
action_items: Ravi Shah - run KV-cache eviction stress matrix and upload results - 2027-01-11
Daniel Park - finalize kernel fallback ordering for Slate Prime and commit config - 2027-01-12
Lena Cho - update launch checklist with third-party driver gating and signoffs - 2027-01-10
Sofia Grant - plan 30-min rollback drill and invite oncall - 2027-01-15
summary: Internal launch-readiness working session for internal codename 'Slate Prime'. Focus: trimming third-party dependency surface, finalizing fallback sequencing, validating bench results for 95th/99th latency, and clarifying runbook owners for the first 72 hours post-launch.
topics: Dependency pruning and vendor driver gating
Kernel fallback ordering and quant skew mitigation
Latency SLOs and 99th percentile stress tests
Compliance signoff path for private deployables
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Ok folks, thanks for joining, we'll kick off — agenda is tight, 64 minutes on the calendar, um, I want to run through the dependency surgery plan, the fallback ordering, and the checklist gaps that Theo flagged.
[00:18] Lena Cho: Quick note, I added the latest slate-prime-checklist in the doc, link in chat, but it's got the old kernel ordering so we need to update that after Daniel's findings.
[00:34] Ravi Shah: (laughs) yeah the old ordering dies in high concurrency, we saw the 2.7x latency blip on the canary run. I'm going to share the full CSV but TL;DR eviction + small-batch fallback helped.
[00:48] Chen Zhao: question on eviction — are we talking prefix/KV cache eviction or full shard compaction? because the latter impacts cold-starts heavy.
[01:05] Ravi Shah: Mostly prefix/KV cache eviction, we used a sliding window of 45s and that kept hot contexts alive; full shard compaction is a heavier hammer and not planned for launch.
[01:20] Omar Ruiz: Are we confident the quantized model variant won't introduce skew at the high tail? Last time we saw small hallucinations at 99th.
[01:34] Daniel Park: We're re-running the quality regressions on the new quant profile, but initial diffs are within tolerance. The bigger risk is kernel fallback ordering causing cross-variant tokenization mismatches — that's what I mean by "surgery" on dependencies, we need to make sure runtime kernel selection doesn't swap code paths mid-sequence.
[01:55] Maya Li: Can you explain that in plain terms? like customer-visible failure mode?
[02:04] Daniel Park: Sure — imagine request A starts on optimized kernel path X, gets partially served, then due to resource pressure it falls back to path Y with slightly different tokenization rules; you get garbled continuation or a safety transform mismatch.
[02:22] Priya Nair: From compliance POV we need a deterministic fallback trace in the audit logs — timestamps and decision reasons. Is that captured today?
[02:35] Ravi Shah: Not fully. We capture high-level fallback events but not the per-token kernel-choice trace. We can add an opt-in verbose trace for dedicated/private customers — cost of logs is the tradeoff.
[02:50] Ava Martinez: Action item: add kernel-choice trace as opt-in flag for dedicated installs, estimate cost and privacy surface — owner Ravi, due Mon 1/11.
[03:04] (typing noises)
[03:20] Theo Martins: I ran a synthetic 1M token run yesterday, worst-case 99th jumped when we hit driver GC on the host. Link to bench in chat — looks like the third-party driver does a stop-the-world compaction and that's correlated.
[03:37] Lena Cho: So dependency surgery is removing that driver or moving it behind a throttled path?
[03:45] Daniel Park: Two levers: vendor driver upgrade (if they can provide non-blocking GC) or swap to our light-weight shim that reduces memory churn. Both have pros/cons. Upgrading vendor is faster but less control; shim gives control but more engineering cost.
[04:04] Omar Ruiz: Prefer shim for enterprise/private customers; for hosted we can gate on the vendor patch to avoid extra maintenance.
[04:15] Sofia Grant: We need to decide by 1/12 to lock rollout codepaths. If we delay, we push the launch window.
[04:28] Ava Martinez: Ok locked decision deadline 1/12. Next — rollback drill. Sofia?
[04:34] Sofia Grant: The plan is a 30-minute drill, simulated traffic with staged degradation: step 1 remove quant variant, step 2 reduce concurrency on slots, step 3 regional failover. We want the oncall team to hit the runbook and validate the postmortem hooks.
[04:56] Chen Zhao: Can we include a fast-rollback toggle in the control plane? We had 8 minutes lost last time to manual config edits.
[05:08] Daniel Park: There's a low-risk toggle in the console; need to add a playbook step so whoever flips it also runs a smoke test queue.
[05:21] Theo Martins: Also, ensure our canary traffic includes safety prompts — the bench doesn't capture prompt engineering edge cases.
[05:36] (crosstalk)
[05:40] Maya Li: On launch metrics — what are the acceptance criteria? I remember we said 99th < 1.2s for the small chat path and < 2.4s for long-context.
[05:53] Ravi Shah: Those are still our targets. Current canary: small chat 99th at 1.35s on vendor driver, 1.05s on shim. Long-context tail is more complicated because KV-cache thrashing affects both.
[06:12] Lena Cho: We should add a canary that exercises long-context patterns for at least 30 minutes at sustained QPS. Priya, any compliance gating on duration?
[06:24] Priya Nair: Nothing specific on duration but we need artifacted test results and signed-off checklist for private deployments prior to customer handover.
[06:35] Ava Martinez: Noted — checklist update (Lena) by 1/10.
[06:40] (pause)
[07:02] Daniel Park: On kernel fallback ordering — I'm proposing fallback order: 1) small-batch optimized kernel, 2) fallback to generic kernel with KV-preserving path, 3) last resort CPU-path. The critical thing: preserve tokenization & KV format between steps.
[07:28] Ravi Shah: If we preserve KV format we can fast-switch without regenerating cache; that's cheaper. But it requires compatibility layer.
[07:40] Daniel Park: Which is doable as a shim, that's part of the surgery.
[07:44] Ava Martinez: Risk register — add entry for "KV format compatibility shim" with severity high and mitigation cost estimate.
[07:55] (writing sounds)
[08:06] Sofia Grant: On the staged degradation messaging — Ops needs a clear user-facing statement: degraded vs offline. Who writes that?
[08:15] Maya Li: Product will draft an initial message; legal/compliance will review. Theo will provide examples from prior incidents.
[08:26] Theo Martins: I'll paste earlier snippets into the doc.
[08:32] Lena Cho: Another dependency: third-party cert rotation library — we saw intermittent TLS renegotiation causing 502s in the canary. Patch available but requires a rolling restart.
[08:45] Omar Ruiz: Rolling restart needs to be in the runbook with step to avoid concurrent eviction across shards.
[08:54] Daniel Park: We'll sequence restarts by ring and ensure the persistent KV is warmed.
[09:03] (sigh)
[09:20] Ravi Shah: Bench share: two CSVs — one with vendor-driver baseline, one with shim. I'll upload both. Key metric to look at: 99.9th per-instance, not just per-aggregated cluster.
[09:37] Ava Martinez: Please annotate which runs include the GC-heavy pattern.
[09:43] Ravi Shah: Will do.
[09:48] (pause)
[10:12] Lena Cho: Timeline check — if we finalize surgery decision by 1/12, engineering invests two sprints for the shim, but we can gate shim to private customers first and vendor patch for hosted.
[10:28] Omar Ruiz: That hybrid approach reduces blast radius. Agree.
[10:33] Priya Nair: Compliance note — private customers may require the shim code review and SCA prior to install, add that to the timeline.
[10:45] Ava Martinez: Add to checklist.
[10:49] Theo Martins: QA needs a test plan for the shim vs vendor path — include adversarial prompt sets.
[10:59] Daniel Park: We'll reuse the adversarial set from the kernel-fallback study.
[11:07] (typing)
[11:20] Sofia Grant: Rollout cadence: phased across regions over 48 hours with telemetry gates at each 4-hour mark. If at any gate 99th increases more than 15% we abort and trigger rollback.
[11:36] Maya Li: That seems reasonable. Make sure runbook has who triggers abort and who communicates externally.
[11:45] Ava Martinez: Communication owner for external status: Maya, with support from Omar. Internal ops comm: Sofia.
[11:54] (notes)
[12:10] Ravi Shah: Small note on cost: shim increases per-token CPU cost by ~3% but reduces tail latency, so net unit-cost might go down because less retrying. We'll model both.
[12:25] Lena Cho: Add cost modeling to the next bench deliverable.
[12:30] Ava Martinez: Action items recap — Ravi will upload annotated benches; Daniel will finalize fallback ordering; Lena updates checklist; Sofia schedules rollback drill. We also need the vendor conversation — someone to own that?
[12:46] Omar Ruiz: I'll own vendor dialog, immediate sync with vendor engineering set for Tue 1/12.
[12:55] Priya Nair: I'll prepare a compliance-readout template for private installs.
[13:05] Ava Martinez: Great. Any final concerns?
[13:10] Chen Zhao: Just flagging the monitoring dashboards — we need a new 99th-per-variant dashboard tile.
[13:20] Sofia Grant: We'll add that to the sprint for next week.
[13:28] (end)
